name: ADF4350BCPZ-RL7
title: Wideband fractional-N/integer-N synthesizer with integrated VCO, 137.5 MHz to 4400 MHz
summary: The ADF4350 is a PLL frequency synthesizer with its VCO on chip. The VCO covers 2200 MHz to 4400 MHz and output dividers of 1 to 16 take the output down to 137.5 MHz. It runs fractional-N with a 12-bit modulus or integer-N, with a reference up to 250 MHz, a PFD up to 32 MHz, an external loop filter, two programmable-power differential outputs, lock detect, fast lock and cycle slip reduction, all set over a 3-wire interface from 3.0 V to 3.6 V.
key_figures: 137.5 MHz to 4400 MHz (VCO 2200 MHz to 4400 MHz)
-4 dBm to +5 dBm in 3 dB steps
-134 dBc/Hz typ at 1 MHz offset, 2.2 GHz and 3.3 GHz
21 mA + 70 mA + 21 mA typ (digital/analog, VCO, RF output)

pins.name: CLK
pins.function: Serial clock. Each rising edge shifts one bit into the 32-bit register. High-impedance CMOS input.

pins.name: DATA
pins.function: Serial data, MSB first; the final three bits are the control bits that pick the register. High-impedance CMOS input.

pins.name: LE
pins.function: Load enable, CMOS. On its rising edge the shift register contents go to the register named by the three LSBs.

pins.name: CE
pins.function: Chip enable. Low: the device powers down and the charge pump goes three-state. High: the device powers up, subject to the power-down bits.

pins.name: SW
pins.function: Fast-lock switch. Connect to the loop filter when fast-lock mode is used.

pins.name: VP
pins.function: Charge pump supply; equal to AVDD. Decouple to the ground plane right at the pin.

pins.name: CPOUT
pins.function: Charge pump output, ±ICP into the external loop filter, whose output goes to VTUNE.

pins.name: CPGND
pins.function: Ground return for CPOUT.

pins.name: AGND
pins.function: Analog ground; return for AVDD.

pins.name: AVDD
pins.function: Analog supply, 3.0 V to 3.6 V, same value as DVDD. Decouple to the analog ground plane right at the pin.

pins.name: AGNDVCO
pins.function: VCO analog ground returns.

pins.name: RFOUTA+
pins.function: Main VCO output, programmable level; carries the fundamental or a divided version.

pins.name: RFOUTA−
pins.function: Complement of RFOUTA+, programmable level; fundamental or divided.

pins.name: RFOUTB+
pins.function: Auxiliary VCO output, programmable level; fundamental or divided.

pins.name: RFOUTB−
pins.function: Complement of RFOUTB+, programmable level; fundamental or divided.

pins.name: VVCO
pins.function: VCO supply, 3.0 V to 3.6 V, same value as AVDD. Decouple to the analog ground plane right at the pins.

pins.name: TEMP
pins.function: Temperature compensation output. Decouple to the ground plane right at the pin.

pins.name: VTUNE
pins.function: VCO control voltage, which sets the output frequency; it is the filtered CPOUT voltage.

pins.name: RSET
pins.function: Charge pump current set: a resistor from RSET to GND gives ICP = 25.5/RSET, so 5.1 kΩ gives 5 mA. Nominal pin bias 0.55 V.

pins.name: VCOM
pins.function: Internal compensation node, held at the middle of the tuning range. Decouple to the ground plane right at the pin.

pins.name: VREF
pins.function: Reference voltage. Decouple to the ground plane right at the pin.

pins.name: LD
pins.function: Lock detect: high when the PLL is locked, low when lock is lost.

pins.name: PDBRF
pins.function: RF power-down. Low mutes the RF outputs; a register bit does the same.

pins.name: DGND
pins.function: Digital ground; return for DVDD.

pins.name: DVDD
pins.function: Digital supply, same voltage as AVDD. Decouple to the ground plane right at the pin.

pins.name: REFIN
pins.function: Reference input. CMOS, threshold nominally VDD/2, dc input resistance about 100 kΩ. Accepts ac coupling, or direct drive from a CMOS or TTL crystal oscillator.

pins.name: MUXOUT
pins.function: Multiplexer output; brings out lock detect, the divided RF or the divided reference, as Register 2 selects.

pins.name: SDGND
pins.function: Ground return for the digital Σ-Δ modulator.

pins.name: SDVDD
pins.function: Supply for the digital Σ-Δ modulator, same voltage as AVDD. Decouple to the ground plane right at the pin.

pins.name: EP
pins.function: Exposed pad; connect to GND.

circuits.title: Fast-lock loop filter, topology 1
circuits.description: A passive loop filter from CPOUT to VTUNE: C1 to ground at CPOUT, C2 in series with a split damping resistor to ground, then R2 in series and C3 to ground at VTUNE. The damping resistor is two pieces, R1 above and R1A below, at a ratio of 1:3, and SW connects to the point between them. In fast-lock mode SW shorts that point to ground, leaving only R1, a quarter of the full damping resistance, while the charge pump current rises 16 times.

circuits.title: Fast-lock loop filter, topology 2
circuits.description: The same passive filter from CPOUT to VTUNE, with the damping resistor R1 whole from C2 to ground. An extra resistor R1A runs from the C2-R1 junction to SW. When fast lock grounds SW, R1A sits in parallel with R1, and R1A is chosen so the pair comes to one quarter of R1.

parts.note: R1A in parallel with R1 equals R1/4

operation.text: A fractional-N or integer-N PLL with the VCO on chip; the loop filter and reference are external. The VCO core is three VCOs of 16 overlapping bands each, covering 2200 MHz to 4400 MHz at the fundamental, and output dividers of 1, 2, 4, 8 or 16 reach down to 137.5 MHz. A main and an auxiliary differential RF output are provided. Everything is set through a 3-wire serial interface from a 3.0 V to 3.6 V supply.

REFIN feeds a buffer through switches. In power-down the input switches open and a third switch closes, so REFIN is not loaded. The R counter (1 to 1023) divides the reference for the PFD; an optional doubler ahead of it and an optional divide-by-2 after it set the PFD rate. With the doubler on, REFIN is limited to 30 MHz, and in low spur mode in-band noise can worsen by up to 5 dB when REFIN duty cycle falls outside 45% to 55%. With the doubler off only the falling edge of REFIN is used at the PFD; with it on, both edges are.

The feedback divide is INT + FRAC/MOD through a third-order fractional interpolator. With FRAC = 0 and LDF (Register 2 DB8) set to 1 the part runs integer-N, and LDF = 1 is also required for integer-N digital lock detect. The 4/5 prescaler is limited to 3 GHz with INT from 23; above 3 GHz the 8/9 prescaler is needed and INT starts at 75.

operation.topic: Phase frequency detector and charge pump
operation.text: The PFD compares the R and N counter outputs. A fixed delay sets an antibacklash pulse of about 3 ns, removing the dead zone and keeping the reference spur steady. The PFD may not exceed 32 MHz because of the speed of the Σ-Δ circuit; doubling the PFD rate usually improves noise by about 3 dB. Charge pump current is set by RSET and by the 4-bit setting in Register 2, which must match the current the loop filter was designed for. PD polarity (DB6) is 1 for a passive or non-inverting active filter and 0 for an inverting active filter.

32 bits are shifted in MSB first on CLK rising edges and moved to one of six registers on the LE rising edge, chosen by the three LSBs. Modulus, phase, R counter, doubler, divide-by-2 and charge pump current are double buffered: a new value is used only after a following write to R0. The R4 divider select is double buffered too, but only while R2 DB13 is 1. After a change of modulus, R0 must be written.

On power-up and on every R0 write the band select logic picks the VCO and band, with VTUNE disconnected from the loop filter and held at an internal reference. It is clocked by the R counter output through a divider of 1 to 255 (R4 BS8:BS1); with a PFD above 125 kHz the divider must be set so band selection has time to finish. Normal loop action then resumes.

KV is 33 MHz/V nominal when the N divider is fed straight from the VCO, or 33 MHz/V divided by the output divider value when it is fed from the divider output. KV varies inside each band and from band to band; 33 MHz/V is the average and best for wideband designs, while the KV against frequency curve suits narrowband designs. On-chip linearization keeps ICP × KV, and so loop bandwidth, nearly constant.

At a fixed frequency VTUNE moves with ambient temperature and, going from hot to cold, can fall below 0.25 V and lose lock. This only happens at fundamental VCO frequencies under 2.95 GHz with ambient below 0°C. Writing R0 again picks a better band; repeat after each further drop of more than 20°C below 0°C. Rising temperature needs no rewrite.

RFOUTA+ and RFOUTA− are the open collectors of an NPN differential pair fed from the VCO buffer or divider. Its tail current, set by R4 D2:D1, gives four power levels: -4, -1, +2 and +5 dBm into a 50 Ω load with a 50 Ω pull-up to AVDD and ac coupling. A 1 + 1:1 transformer or a 180° microstrip coupler may join the two sides. Used single-ended, the best load is a shunt inductor to VVCO, with the unused side terminated the same way. RFOUTB± is a second differential output that can be powered down; it works only while the main output is on. With MTLD set (R4 DB10) the output stage stays unpowered until digital lock detect shows lock.

MUXOUT, set by R2 M3:M1, shows three-state, DVDD, DGND, the R divider output, the N divider output, analog lock detect or digital lock detect. The LD pin, set by R5 DB23:DB22, gives digital lock detect or a fixed low or high. Fractional-N digital lock detect (LDF = 0) needs 40 PFD cycles in a row within 10 ns with LDP = 0, or within 6 ns with LDP = 1. Integer-N lock detect (LDF = 1) needs five cycles in a row: within 6 ns with LDP = 0, within 10 ns with LDP = 1.

R2 DB30:DB29 choose low noise or low spur mode. Low spur mode turns on dither, which spreads fractional quantization noise into a noise floor; it suits wide loop bandwidths (more than one tenth of the output channel step) used for fast lock, where the filter attenuates spurs less. Low noise mode turns dither off and runs the charge pump where it is quietest, best with a narrow loop that filters the spurs. In low spur mode MOD must be at least 50, and in-band noise can rise by up to 10 dB.

CE low powers the device down and three-states the charge pump. Software power-down (R2 DB5 = 1) keeps the registers; they are lost only when supplies are removed. In power-down the counters go to their load state, the VCO stops, the charge pump goes three-state, digital lock detect resets and the RF output buffers turn off, while the input register still accepts data. R2 DB4 = 1 three-states the charge pump and must be 0 in normal operation; R2 DB3 = 1 holds the R and N counters in reset and must be 0 in normal operation. R4 DB11 powers the VCO down. Low power sleep current is 7 µA typ.

R4 DB23 = 1 takes the N divider feedback straight from the VCO; 0 takes it from the output divider. With the feedback after the divider, the outputs of two separately programmed PLLs come out in phase, which helps where signals are combined to add power.
Once the supplies are up, write the registers in the order R5, R4, R3, R2, R1, R0.

MOD is set over a 12-bit range, so one fixed PFD rate can serve several channel steps. For 1.75 GHz with 200 kHz steps from 13 MHz, MOD = 65 at a 13 MHz PFD works, and the doubler to 26 MHz with MOD = 130 works with lower phase noise. A dual-mode phone keeps a 13 MHz PFD and switches MOD between 520 (25 kHz, PDC) and 65 (200 kHz, GSM 1800), so one loop filter suits both; the loop design depends on the RF to PFD ratio, not on the channel step.

When the loop bandwidth is narrow compared with the PFD rate, phase error can build up faster than the loop corrects and the charge pump briefly drives the wrong way, slowing lock badly. With CSR on (R3 DB18 = 1), each time a slip is about to happen the chip adds a constant-current charge pump cell, up to seven, then removes them one by one once the VCO passes the target, leaving the original loop bandwidth. The PFD input needs a 45% to 55% duty cycle (RDIV2 gives 50%), and the charge pump current must be at its minimum setting.

Fast lock widens the loop for a set time and then returns to a narrow loop that keeps spurs low. Set R3 DB16:DB15 to 0, 1 and load the timer in DB14:DB3 after the one-time initialization. During the wide-bandwidth period the charge pump current rises 16 times and SW is shorted to ground, which must cut the damping resistance to a quarter to stay stable. Example: 13 MHz reference and PFD, MOD = 65 for 200 kHz, 50 µs lock target, 40 µs wide, timer value 8; VCO band select time is extra.

Fractional spurs come from the Σ-Δ quantization: with dither off they repeat at fPFD/L, L depending on MOD, and with dither on L is 2^21 and the spurs become broadband noise. For lowest noise, dither off is preferred when the final loop is narrow enough to attenuate the lowest fractional spur. Integer boundary spurs appear at the beat between the VCO frequency and the nearest integer multiple of the reference, and show on channels near those multiples, where the beat falls inside the loop bandwidth. Reference spurs from on-chip reference switching noise coupling through the RF input back to the VCO can reach -90 dBc; keep VCO traces well isolated from the reference input.

With dither disabled, the spur pattern from quantization also depends on the phase word that seeds the modulator. A table of phase values per frequency can tune fractional and subfractional spurs; without one, hold the phase word constant so each frequency always gives the same spurs. When neither phase resync nor spur tuning is used, set PHASE to 1.

A fractional-N loop may settle at any of MOD phase offsets to the reference. With R3 DB16:DB15 = 1, 0 an internal timer issues sync pulses every tSYNC, and the second pulse after LE rises realigns the output phase to the reference, giving a repeatable offset for uses such as digital beam forming. Set tSYNC to at least the worst-case lock time so the resync follows the last cycle slip. Sweeping the PHASE word from 0 to MOD then steps the output phase over 360° in steps of 360°/MOD.
θJA is 27.3°C/W with the paddle soldered. Junction limit 150°C; reflow peak 260°C, 40 s at peak.
